newsitem.title: UK: Philippines blossoms in emerging debt trading.
newsitem.headline: Philippines blossoms in emerging debt trading.

text.p: East European and other non-Latin American debt on Tuesday caught up with New York's late Brady market rise, and the Philippines showed the biggest gain.
The market bounce in New York the previous day was led by Ecuador after talk of a possible $300 million Eurobond.

"Latins were well-bid this morning but unchanged. The rest of the market moved up simply to catch up," said one U.S. bank trader, adding trading was very quiet in the run-up to the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.
Philippine pars PH425L18=RR rose more than a point to a bid of 90-1/4 cents in the dollar on what the trader called delayed reaction to last Friday's signing of an important tax reform bill.
"It has been a sticking point with the ratings agencies and this could be the precursor to an upgrade," he said.
But a Standard & Poor's executive at the weekend warned that the country's heavy debt burden would go against a review of its rating.

Russia was also firmer, as Vneshekonombank paper edged up 1/4 of a point, undeterred by news that an International Monetary Fund mission would leave Moscow on Tuesday without a decision on whether to pay out the latest tranche of a $10 billion loan.
Traders said the view on Russia remains very firm though there is little news at present to drive the market much higher.
Prices for Vnesh are currently about four points below their record high in early October.
Bulgaria was flat after Monday's brief surge on news that Prime Minister Zhan Videnov had accepted the IMF's proposal to introduce a currency board.
Details of the scheme have yet to be presented and some analysts doubt it would be a panacea for the crumbling economy.
